value: Counts toward MAGI
detail: Taxable interest is included in AGI; tax-exempt interest is added back for MAGI. Marketplace and Medicaid rules both count expected interest and dividends on investments.
source_name: Healthcare.gov - What is included as income

value: Counts toward MAGI (use net rental and royalty income)
detail: Net rental income (rents minus expenses, as reported on Schedule E) flows into AGI and therefore MAGI for Medi-Cal and premium tax credits.
source_name: Healthcare.gov - What is included as income

value: Generally passive (unearned)
detail: Rental real estate is generally a passive activity; losses are limited by passive-activity rules, with an up-to-$25,000 special allowance for active participants (phasing out at higher income) and an exception for qualifying real estate professionals.

value: Self-employment (earned) income if you are paid to manage property for others
detail: Report real-estate rentals on Schedule E; if you provide substantial services primarily for tenants' convenience, report on Schedule C instead. Fees for managing property you do not own are business (self-employment) income; rent from property you own is rental income. Therefore a person who actually receives third-party management fees has earned/self-employment income for that activity - report it accurately rather than as $0 earned income.
source_name: IRS Topic No. 414 - Rental income and expenses
notes: The user reports $0 earned income, implying self-managed owned property and/or no third-party fees. If management fees are received, both tax filing and the work-rule analysis change.

value: Taxable income; counts toward MAGI
detail: Gains from trading on Kalshi are taxable and included in AGI/MAGI regardless of their federal tax character. Kalshi issues 1099-INT (interest), 1099-MISC (credits/rewards), 1099-B (crypto transfer proceeds), and 1099-DA (digital assets via ZeroHash), plus a monthly-updated P&L statement; Kalshi states its information is not tax advice.
source_name: Kalshi Help Center - What Tax Documentation Does Kalshi Provide?
notes: Kalshi does not issue a comprehensive 1099 for event-contract trading itself.

value: CFTC-regulated Designated Contract Market (DCM)
detail: Kalshi is regulated by the Commodity Futures Trading Commission as a DCM - an exchange designated to trade futures, swaps, and options on commodities.
source_name: Kalshi Help Center - How is Kalshi regulated?

value: 60% long-term / 40% short-term capital gain; year-end mark-to-market; Form 6781
detail: Contracts that qualify as section 1256 contracts are marked to market at year-end and taxed 60% as long-term and 40% as short-term capital gain regardless of holding period.

item: Whether Kalshi event contracts qualify as section 1256 contracts
detail: No IRS ruling or published guidance classifies Kalshi event contracts as section 1256 contracts; the tax character (section 1256 vs. capital asset vs. other) is unsettled and Kalshi itself takes no position. See Flagged for Review.
notes: Value left blank intentionally: cannot be confirmed from an official source. See flagged item FL-01. Regardless of character, gains are unearned investment income that counts in MAGI.

item: Earned vs. unearned income for MAGI
value: Both count
detail: For Medi-Cal and premium tax credits, household MAGI includes both earned income (wages, net self-employment) and unearned income (interest, dividends, capital gains, net rental, retirement).
source_name: Healthcare.gov - What is included as income

value: Offset gains; up to $3,000 per year against other income; carryforward
detail: If capital losses (including trading losses) exceed capital gains, up to $3,000 per year is deductible against other income with the remainder carried forward - this lowers AGI and therefore MAGI in loss years.

value: $580 MAGI-based income in a qualifying month (any source, including unearned) satisfies the work rule for that month
detail: DHCS member outreach letter: income from any source of at least $580 (before taxes) in any month since the last renewal meets the rule. Federal regulation 42 CFR 435.552(f) defines the test as monthly income measured on a MAGI basis for the individual's MAGI household - so net rental income, interest (including tax-exempt added back in MAGI), and net capital/trading gains are the relevant measure, not gross rents or gross trade proceeds and not wages only. Six-month averaging: see WR-06/FL-11 (federal seasonal-worker limit vs broader DHCS wording).
notes: How a county documents monthly MAGI for volatile trading P&L (realized gains/losses by month) is not yet published - see FL-06. Keep monthly records by source.

item: Whose income counts for the $580 test
value: The individual's MAGI-based income for their MAGI-based household (42 CFR 435.552(f)(2); CA Welf. & Inst. Code 14005.69(e)(6))
detail: This supersedes the preliminary ACWDL 25-30 'total gross income' phrasing (Dec 2025, before the federal rule). The June 2026 federal regulation and California's AB 2161 both measure the $580 test with MAGI-based methods for the individual's MAGI household budget. ACWDL also states eligibility/compliance is assessed individually - one person's compliance cannot satisfy another's. For multi-person households, the federal rule requires a reasonable allocation method when converting household income to an individual's work hours (435.552(e)(2)); California's allocation procedure is not yet published.
notes: Re-verified 2026-10-18 (session da6d01ac) against eCFR and chaptered AB 2161 text. Resolves gross-vs-net in favor of MAGI (net rental, net gains). Remaining: monthly measurement of trading gains/losses and household allocation - FL-06.

detail: Not addressed in official materials. Federal work includes paid/in-kind/unpaid work and (per CMS preamble and DHCS ACWDL) self-employment, but no official source states whether hours spent trading one's own Kalshi/futures account qualify. Separately, IRS guidance says gains/losses from trading securities for one's own account are not self-employment earnings subject to SE tax even for a qualifying trader (Topic 429) - that tax rule explains $0 earned income but does not by itself decide the Medicaid 'work' question. See Flagged for Review.
notes: Value left blank intentionally. See flagged item FL-02. Safe verified alternatives: the $580 MAGI-based income standard in a qualifying month, 80 hours of structured community service, or at least half-time school.

value: AGI + untaxed foreign income + non-taxable Social Security benefits + tax-exempt interest
detail: MAGI does not include SSI; for many people MAGI equals or is close to AGI.

value: Taxable interest, net capital gains, rental or royalty income (profit after costs), self-employment net income all counted
detail: CMS MAGI training materials list the taxable income counted in determining Medicaid/CHIP MAGI-based income.

value: Trading gains/losses for your own account are NOT self-employment earnings (no SE tax), even for a qualifying trader
detail: IRS Topic No. 429: a trader in securities buys/sells for their own account as a trade or business only if facts-and-circumstances tests are met (profit from daily movements, substantial activity, continuity/regularity) - calling yourself a trader does not decide it. Traders deduct business expenses on Schedule C, but gains and losses from selling securities are not subject to self-employment tax; investors' investment income likewise is not SE income. With or without a section 475(f) mark-to-market election, trading profit therefore does not become wages/earned SE income merely because trading is full-time.
source_name: IRS Topic No. 429 - Traders in securities
notes: IRS Publication 550 states the same no-SE-tax rule for traders in securities or commodities (with a dealer/section 1256 exception discussion). This tax characterization is consistent with reporting $0 earned income; it does not determine Medi-Cal MAGI (gains still count) or whether trading hours are Medicaid 'work' (FL-02).

value: Rental real-estate income is generally NOT net earnings from self-employment
detail: IRS Schedule E instructions: rental real estate income is generally not included in net earnings from self-employment subject to SE tax and is generally subject to passive-loss limits. Managing your own rentals therefore ordinarily produces (unearned) rental income, not earned income - consistent with $0 earned income. Contrast IN-04: substantial tenant services or managing others' property for fees can be Schedule C business/SE income.
notes: Whether hours managing your own rentals count as Medicaid 'work' is a separate, unresolved county question (FL-12).

item: Medi-Cal uses current monthly MAGI; lump sums count only in the month received
value: Monthly (point-in-time) MAGI budget period for Medicaid; taxable lump sum counted only in month received
detail: 42 CFR 435.603(h) bases Medicaid financial eligibility for applicants/new enrollees on current monthly household income and family size, and 435.603(e)(1) counts an amount received as a lump sum as income only in the month received. Practical effect for volatile income: a large realized trading gain concentrated in one month can affect that month's Medi-Cal MAGI (and can also supply the $580 qualifying month), while Covered California/PTC instead uses estimated annual MAGI reconciled at tax filing. Monthly documentation matters; ask the county how they budget recurring trading/rental receipts vs one-time amounts.
notes: Qualified lottery/gambling winnings of $80,000+ have a separate statutory spreading rule; no determination is made here that Kalshi contracts are gambling/lottery winnings - get tax/county advice for large wins.

item: Whose income counts for the $580 test
value: The individual's own total gross income for a month
detail: DHCS ACWDL 25-30 qualifying-activities table, 'Income equivalent to at least 80 hours at federal minimum wage (currently $7.25 per hour x 80 hours). Currently, this amount is $580 a month': 'An individual's total gross income for a month must meet or exceed this amount.'
notes: Labelled preliminary guidance by DHCS. ACWDL 25-30 also states Medi-Cal eligibility is determined at the individual level and one individual's compliance cannot satisfy another's.

item: Unearned income explicitly counts toward the $580 test
value: Gross income 'including earned income, unemployment benefits, State Disability Insurance, retirement income, dividends, etc.'
detail: DHCS ACWDL 25-30, fluctuating-income row: 'An individual whose gross income (including earned income, unemployment benefits, State Disability Insurance, retirement income, dividends, etc.) fluctuates has an average monthly income over the preceding 6 months that meets or exceeds this amount.'
notes: No official source lists rental income, savings interest, or trading gains by name - see flagged item FL-17.

item: Gross vs net income for the two different tests
value: MAGI uses net rental and royalty income; the $580 work test is expressed as total gross income
detail: HealthCare.gov instructs Marketplace/Medicaid MAGI filers to 'use net rental and royalty income.' DHCS ACWDL 25-30 describes the $580 standard as 'total gross income for a month.' California statute WIC 14005.69(e)(6) frames it on MAGI-based financial methods for the individual's MAGI-based household budget.
source_name: Healthcare.gov - What is included as income
notes: The three official phrasings are not identical; see flagged items FL-05 and FL-16. The practical difference (gross rent vs net rent) can decide whether a month clears $580 - confirm with the county.

value: Average monthly income over the preceding 6 months at or above $580, for a seasonal worker
detail: DHCS ACWDL 25-30: 'Average monthly income of at least 80 hours at federal minimum wage (currently $580 a month) for individuals with fluctuating income over a six-month period.' California statute WIC 14005.69(e)(7) adds that the individual must be a seasonal worker as described in 26 U.S.C. 45R(d)(5)(B).
notes: DHCS's member page describes this as a seasonal worker earning an average of $580 a month over the last six months.

item: Kalshi tax documentation available to a preparer
value: 1099-INT, 1099-MISC, 1099-B (crypto transfer proceeds), 1099-DA (digital assets via ZeroHash), plus a monthly-updated Profit and Loss statement; FIFO accounting
detail: Kalshi's help center states users who hit IRS reporting thresholds receive those forms, that Kalshi uses FIFO to compute profits and losses, that P&L data is updated on the first morning of each month and includes fees and rebates, that some forms are delivered electronically by Zenwork, and that the information 'are not tax advice, and Kalshi cannot give members advice on their taxes.'
source_name: Kalshi Help Center - What Tax Documentation Does Kalshi Provide?
notes: No form is issued for event-contract trading itself - see flagged item FL-01.
